Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate Dedicated capacity against your production concurrency profile. High-level recap:

- Ask: PipelineApps needs a deterministic commitment for sustained 25 rps (generation requests) with short bursts to 60 rps for 60s, tail latency target p95 < 250ms for prompt sizes ~512 tokens.
- Options discussed: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + burst policy) vs hyperscaler Reserved VMs with autoscaling and spot fallback.
- Differentiators we highlighted: automatic KV/prefix caching, continuous batching tuned to your request distribution, and transparent cost/latency breakdown per model route.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) We run a two-week dedicated PoC using a 3xA10-like reserved pool mirroring your 25rps steady-state with configured burst headroom. Redwood provides SLA target matrix and rollback/fallback policy.
2) PipelineApps runs a short parallel test on your hyperscaler account (we will provide a test script) to compare steady-state latency, cold-start tail behavior, and cost per 1M tokens under identical prompt distribution.
3) Deliverables: a P95/P99 latency report, cost comparison (tokens + infra), and an operational playbook for failover.

Attached: preliminary SLA matrix and the test matrix we discussed.

Can you confirm: (a) whether you can share short-term access to a test project on your hyperscaler or we should spin up equivalent instances under Redwood for apples-to-apples? (b) the dates you prefer for the two-week PoC window (we suggested May 3–17).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus/Monica for technical setup once you confirm.

—Vivek

Sara — thanks. Quick answers inline and added a concrete ask for Marcus/Monica to prepare the test harness: 

1) Minimum config: if you host the hyperscaler side, we ask for equivalently provisioned GPU instances (NVIDIA A10/NVIDIA T4 equivalent) and a small policy to allow our test runner 10 concurrent connections. If Redwood manages the test, we provision a 3 GPU reserved pool that matches the steady-state rps; network egress is accounted separately in the cost table.

2) Guarantees: Redwood Dedicated offers SLA-backed performance tiers. For the PoC we propose a milestone-based acceptance: if P95 > 350ms for steady-state (25 rps) over a 48-hour window during the agreed PoC, Redwood will: (a) provide a prioritized ops time window to tune configs and (b) issue a one-time service credit equal to 10% of the PoC committed capacity cost. For production reserved contracts we can negotiate stronger credits; we will surface formal SLA language in the contract draft. We will also provide an automatic fallback route to our hosted API for short bursts to avoid total outage (configurable).

3) Cost table: attached spreadsheet includes sample rows with and without spot/preemptible, and an approximate network egress estimate. We will refine once you confirm whether to include managed Redwood infra network vs your own cloud egress.

Marcus/Monica — please prepare: test harness that can replay their 30k-sample prompt set, the probing script for burst windows (60s bursts), and a small runbook for how we swap in the fallback hosted route during failure scenarios. Also include suggested telemetry we want on the PipelineApps side (token counts, model name, route id).

Sara — happy to sign the PoC schedule once you confirm the dev project access.

—Vivek

Hi Sara — Marcus here with the technical bits. I built the first-pass test matrix attached (pipeline-test-matrix.csv) and a short README for the runner. Key clarifications and asks: 

- Workloads: we need a representative sample of your prompt mix (short Q/A, medium-form summarization ~512 tokens, and long-form 1k+). The provided sample will be replayed with the same inter-request timings you report (burst windows included).
- Concurrency semantics: Redwood Dedicated keeps an internal request queue and applies continuous batching; for your burst to 60 rps we recommend configuring a burst headroom of 2x steady CPU/GPU to avoid queue pileup.
- Cold start behavior: hyperscaler scale-ups typically show a 500–1,200ms tail when provisioning new VMs; Redwood Dedicated keeps warmed workers and KV cache primed, so cold starts are usually < 120ms for common models. We will measure this in the PoC.
- Metrics we will capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue length, and fallback activations. We’ll output CSV and a short summary report after each test window.

Small asks for PipelineApps dev team: 
1) Provide the sample prompt zip and a service account with read-only run access for the dev project (if you want to host the hyperscaler side).
2) Confirm the acceptable windows for a daytime run (we prefer low-traffic windows so results are stable).

Forwarding the harness README below for convenience.

Thanks — Marcus
